4 ارغدوا They became in a state of life ample in its means or circumstances, unstraitened, or plentiful; (S, A;) they had abundance of herbage, or of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life. (S, K.) ＝
-A2- ارغد ٱللّٰهُ عَيْشَهُمْ God made their life to be ample in its means or circumstances, unstraitened, or plentiful, [and easy,] and pleasant. (A.) ―
-b2- And ارغدوا مَوَاشِيَهُمْ They left their cattle to pasture by themselves, where they pleased. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
